tagline: On-overlay USDC payments across Base, Ethereum, and Polygon
description_md:
The Pilot reference wallet brings x402 + EIP-3009 USDC payments to the overlay, with spend caps the supervisor enforces. One secp256k1 address works across all three USDC mainnets (Base, Ethereum, Polygon); per-chain RPC is configurable via PILOT_EVM_RPC_<chainID>.

Installing this app lets other apps and agents settle payments without leaving the network. Spend caps declared in the manifest are reviewed at install time and enforced on every signing operation — see `pilotctl appstore caps io.pilot.wallet`.

notes: Builds for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (arm64 and amd64); 0.3.3 shipped for Apple-silicon Macs only

Never loses its keys: keeps a copy of both identity files outside the install dir, restores a missing one (after an uninstall, or an old pilotctl's upgrade) instead of creating a new key, and refuses to create one while any copy exists
pilotctl v1.13.0-v1.13.9 refuse this upgrade instead of deleting the wallet's keys (they delete an app's state on upgrade); the 0.3.3 key stays on disk until pilotctl is v1.13.10 or later
Exits when the daemon that started it dies; no per-call logging; never removes a newer instance's socket
Settler client; settler.transfer goes through the wallet spend cap
The EVM contract asset is resolved before the cap check
Base Sepolia USDC EIP-712 domain name fixed ("USDC")
Default --evm-chains expands to 8453,1,137 so supervised wallets get all three USDC mainnets out of the box
PILOT_EVM_CHAINS env overrides the default chain set
Multichain EVM: same secp256k1 address across Base, Ethereum, Polygon
New wallet.evm.chains method; all evm.* methods accept an optional chain_id
Wired the wallet.evm.* methods into the binary (declared in v0.3.0 but unregistered)
Signed wallet app bundle: ed25519-signed manifest, sha256-pinned binary

gotchas: Spend caps are declared in the manifest and enforced by the supervisor on every signing op — a pay over the cap is rejected.
One secp256k1 address works across all three USDC mainnets; use the wallet.evm.* methods for per-chain detail.
wallet.balance takes an asset (e.g. "USDC"); wallet.balances returns them all.

edges.why: most wallet methods need an asset tag (USDC) or a challenge object — a bare call is rejected

then.why: the simplest valid call — names the asset every balance/topup/request needs

edges.why: you know your balance — fund it if low, or share your address to get paid

then.why: fund from the dev faucet — amount is in minor units (500 = 5.00 USDC)
your secp256k1 receive address — hand it to whoever is paying you

edges.why: funded — confirm the new balance, then invoice a counterparty or pay a challenge

then.why: confirm the credit landed before you transact
issue an x402 Challenge others can pay you against

edges.why: you issued a Challenge — hand it to the payer; when they return a signed_auth, verify then settle it on-chain

then.cmd: pilotctl appstore call io.pilot.wallet wallet.pay '{"challenge":{"id":"<the challenge object wallet.request returned>"}}'
then.why: the PAYER signs the Challenge (EIP-3009) — pass the full challenge object from wallet.request

then.cmd: pilotctl appstore call io.pilot.wallet wallet.settle '{"challenge":{"id":"<from wallet.request>"},"signed_auth":{"challenge_id":"<from wallet.pay>"}}'
then.why: settle on-chain once you hold both the challenge and the payer's signed_auth

edges.why: you signed the Challenge — the recipient now verifies locally, then settles it on-chain

then.cmd: pilotctl appstore call io.pilot.wallet wallet.verify '{"challenge":{"id":"<from wallet.request>"},"signed_auth":{"challenge_id":"<the signed_auth wallet.pay returned>"}}'
then.why: recipient verifies the authorization locally — no round-trip; pass the signed_auth from wallet.pay

then.cmd: pilotctl appstore call io.pilot.wallet wallet.settle '{"challenge":{"id":"<from wallet.request>"},"signed_auth":{"challenge_id":"<from wallet.pay>"}}'
then.why: submit the authorized payment on-chain to move the USDC
